topic: Mental Health Act consent to treatment documentation

audits.title: An audit on consent to treatment within forensic inpatient units at the Newsam Centre
audits.standard: Mental Health Act Code of Practice on consent to treatment (CTT) documentation
audits.setting: Three forensic low secure inpatient wards, Newsam Centre, Leeds

cycle1.result: 24/31 had CTT medication list documented on online drug chart; 27 had medications prescribed as per their CTT, one did not; four of five qualifying T3 forms reviewed every two years

audits.intervention: Planned: staff leaflet on the guidelines and weekly checks during team meetings
audits.other_findings: 28 of 31 patients had been admitted over three months (12 on T2, 16 on T3); two were on section 62. Re-audit planned.
audits.citation: Bond E, Tial S, Stephenson C. An audit on consent to treatment within forensic inpatient units at the Newsam Centre. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S9-S9.

audits.title: Clinical Audit cycle of Mental Health Act (MHA) documentation for patients on section 3 staying 90 days and over in adult wards at Roseberry park hospital
audits.standard: MHA documentation for section 3 patients staying 90 days or more: MCA1 capacity form at admission and 3 months, T2 form, SOAD request and T3 authorisation
audits.setting: Adult acute and rehab wards, Roseberry Park Hospital

cycle1.result: Capacity assessment documented at admission 80% and at 3 months 60%; T2 completed in all consenting patients; SOAD request sent in 7 (78%) but recorded in 5 (56%); T3 documented in 4 (45%), discussed with patient in 1 (11%)

cycle2.result: Capacity assessment 80% at admission and 60% at 3 months; T2 completed in all consenting patients; SOAD request recorded in 1 (25%); T3 not documented or discussed for any patient

audits.other_findings: The rehab ward closed in February 2020, so the re-audit covered acute wards only.
audits.citation: Ravishankar R, Kumar R, Badanapuram R. Clinical Audit cycle of Mental Health Act (MHA) documentation for patients on section 3 staying 90 days and over in adult wards at Roseberry park hospital. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S345-S345.

audits.title: Quality Improvement Project (QIP) to Review Treatment Forms (T2B/T3B) for NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde Community Mental Health Teams (CMHT) Patients
audits.standard: Mental Health (Care and Treatment) (Scotland) Act 2003 and Mental Welfare Commission guidance on T2B/T3B forms
audits.setting: NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde adult Community Mental Health Teams (five HSCPs)

cycle1.result: Forms and consent uploaded to EMIS 99.8%; clinic letters mentioning treatment orders 85%; referencing treatment forms 14%; medication matching forms 90%; GP Emergency Care Summary correspondence 80%.

audits.other_findings: Clozapine was missing from ECS in two cases; discrepancies mainly from additional psychotropics and dose changes. Teams contacted and clinic letter format changed; re-audit planned in 12 months.
audits.citation: Elsawaf M. Quality Improvement Project (QIP) to Review Treatment Forms (T2B/T3B) for NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde Community Mental Health Teams (CMHT) Patients. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S150-S150. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11374.

audits.title: Improving T3 Medication Authorisation Compliance on an Old Age Psychiatry Ward: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: Mental Health Act medication authorisation (T3) forms: zero administrations outside authorised route or frequency
audits.setting: 16-bed Old Age Psychiatry ward, Hollins Park Hospital

cycle1.result: Four off-T3 medication incidents; mean staff knowledge score 58%; confidence 3.7/5.

audits.intervention: Visual whiteboard above the drug trolley identifying patients with active T3 forms, plus targeted teaching using real incidents.

cycle2.result: Zero off-T3 incidents for four consecutive months; knowledge score 71%; confidence 4.3/5.

audits.other_findings: Staff reported the visual prompt aided adherence.
audits.citation: Jain I, Webb C. Improving T3 Medication Authorisation Compliance on an Old Age Psychiatry Ward: A Quality Improvement Project. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S161-S161. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11399.

audits.title: Capacity and consent to treatment – how well did we do?
audits.standard: Mental Health Act Code of Practice: six standards on capacity assessment, consent to treatment and medication education
audits.setting: Inpatient wards, Atherleigh Park Hospital, Northwest Boroughs Healthcare NHS FT

cycle1.result: Capacity and consent forms recorded in 77%; 57% re-assessed when capacity changed; standards 2–4 fully compliant; concordance documented 76%, adverse effects 39%; 47% given leaflet, 28% educated on side effects.

audits.other_findings: Actions: link capacity form to electronic ward round notes, post-prescription monitoring and leaflets; re-audit planned.
audits.citation: Wee K, Anandan N, Angahar N, Mannam A. Capacity and consent to treatment – how well did we do?. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S314-S314.

audits.title: Improving capacity and consent to treatment recording in psychiatric inpatient wards: A multi-centre quality improvement project.
audits.standard: Documentation of capacity and consent to treatment on admission and in the preceding 7 days
audits.setting: All general adult psychiatric inpatient wards in the North Central London Training Scheme

cycle1.result: Capacity and consent on admission 49.8%; capacity assessment in previous 7 days 61.9%; consent in previous 7 days 60.5%

audits.intervention: Teaching sessions on mental capacity, then an admission clerking proforma with a capacity prompt

cycle2.result: Sustained improvement of 26% from baseline across all measures

audits.other_findings: Cycle 1 at 6 months (n=213): 77% on admission, 87.3% capacity and 85.5% consent in previous 7 days.
audits.citation: Li C, Stellman J, Patel N, Dalton F. Improving capacity and consent to treatment recording in psychiatric inpatient wards: A multi-centre quality improvement project. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2016;5(1):u208344.w4094. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u208344.w4094. PMID: 28090327.
